name: Desk Buddy
tagline: A little company for the next thing.
description: Write three small steps and tick them off yourself. The working local checklist updates your companion as you make progress, resets a check when its wording changes, and exports the list as a text keepsake.
audience: Solo makers, students, and anyone starting a small piece of work

companionBehavior.idle: Visual direction: The original Noun rests above an empty desk line; one quiet dot marks readiness.
companionBehavior.working: Visual direction: Three squares fill beneath the unchanged portrait as you complete the checklist.
companionBehavior.needsYou: Visual direction: An amber corner flag appears beside the next unfinished step; the Noun stays still.
companionBehavior.complete: Visual direction: The desk line becomes a terracotta frame and a dated completion seal appears.

firstBuild: Three editable steps, completion toggles, uncheck-all control, and a downloadable checklist.
expansion: Companion themes, reusable work rituals, and a wall of completed session cards.
artifact: A text checklist recording your entered steps and their manually selected completion states.
exampleTask: Prepare one shrine collection for a first paper proof.
futureConnection: An authorized task-list connector could read real task progress later. This demo has no task-service connection and does not perform the task for you.

name: Scout
description: Compare up to three ideas or leads using three equally weighted criteria you choose. The local tool ranks your entered scores and calls out ties; it does not browse, research, or verify the candidates.
audience: Researchers, buyers, curators, and curious collectors

companionBehavior.idle: Visual direction: The Noun waits beside a single compass point on a quiet field.
companionBehavior.working: Visual direction: A three-stop route draws around the unchanged portrait as you mark leads reviewed.
companionBehavior.needsYou: Visual direction: One route stop gains a question marker when you flag an unsupported claim.
companionBehavior.complete: Visual direction: The route closes into a map frame with a visible count of reviewed leads.

firstBuild: Editable criteria and candidate names, three scores per candidate, a ranked comparison, and a text report.
expansion: Dated evidence cards, source links, weighting controls, and trails through collection archives.
artifact: A comparison report with your criteria, entered scores, ranking, and a clear note that the inputs are yours.
exampleTask: Compare three paper stocks using your own scores for fold quality, availability, and cost.
futureConnection: A future authorized search tool could retrieve sources and preserve their links and dates. External search and independent verification are not part of the local demo.

name: Keeper
tagline: Keep a thought before it slips away.
description: Keep up to twelve short notes in this browser tab, delete individual entries, or export the notebook as text. Session storage preserves the notes across a reload in the same tab when available; nothing is sent to a memory service.
audience: Families, artists, archivists, and people giving meaningful gifts

companionBehavior.idle: Visual direction: The Noun sits inside the outline of an open archive sleeve.
companionBehavior.working: Visual direction: Three paper tabs slide into place around the unchanged portrait as fields are completed.
companionBehavior.needsYou: Visual direction: A loose bookmark marks an empty date, attribution, or story field for you to resolve.
companionBehavior.complete: Visual direction: The sleeve closes into a labeled keepsake card with a small archive seal.

firstBuild: A twelve-note session notebook, delete controls, storage-availability feedback, and text export.
expansion: Object stories, provenance fields, collection timelines, and printed archive cards.
artifact: A numbered text notebook containing the notes you chose to keep.
exampleTask: Keep useful observations while reviewing a first paper-temple proof.
futureConnection: An explicitly chosen archive or cloud folder could store and retrieve records later. Persistence and sharing would need visible controls; the concept does not imply a connected long-term memory service.

name: Tempo
tagline: Give a little rhythm to your day.
description: Choose a one-minute or five-minute focus session and an optional intention. Start, pause, resume, or reset the local clock; finishing the interval produces a text receipt. Leaving this project stops its timer.
audience: Writers, designers, makers, and people who prefer a visible work rhythm

companionBehavior.idle: Visual direction: Four empty beat marks sit beside the Noun, ready for a session.
companionBehavior.working: Visual direction: A fine progress arc advances around the unchanged portrait with the visible timer.
companionBehavior.needsYou: Visual direction: The arc becomes a pause symbol when the interval ends or you pause the session.
companionBehavior.complete: Visual direction: Four filled beat marks and the actual elapsed duration form a small session stamp.

firstBuild: One- and five-minute wall-clock timer, intention field, pause/resume/reset controls, and a completion receipt.
expansion: Custom work rhythms, quiet visual themes, and printable weekly rhythm cards.
artifact: A text receipt with the chosen interval, entered focus, and completion time; it is not proof that work occurred.
exampleTask: Spend a short session refining the dedication on a gift set.
futureConnection: Calendar availability or operating-system notifications could be connected with permission later. The local timer is not a background monitoring service and does not block other apps.

name: Muse
description: Choose a mood, a material, an object, an audience, and a constraint. The local tool composes a creative brief and cycles through four layout directions from a fixed library; it does not generate an image.
audience: Artists, creative teams, teachers, and collection designers

companionBehavior.idle: Visual direction: An empty color swatch floats beside the unchanged original Noun.
companionBehavior.working: Visual direction: Three surrounding swatches rearrange when you remix the subject, mood, and material.
companionBehavior.needsYou: Visual direction: Two direction cards open beside the portrait so you can choose which idea to develop.
companionBehavior.complete: Visual direction: The chosen palette settles into a printed proof border with an edition mark.

firstBuild: Mood, material, and object choices; audience and constraint fields; four rotating layout directions; and text export.
expansion: Saved direction boards, collaborator votes, and an optional image-generation handoff with recorded prompts.
artifact: A text creative brief with your choices, a layout direction, and an actual-size proof reminder.
exampleTask: Invent a moonlit Nouns fishing-lure collection in enamel and paper.
futureConnection: A connected image generator could interpret approved briefs later. Exact original Nouns art would remain a separate preserved layer; generated interpretations would be labeled.

name: Sprout
tagline: Let a small idea take root.
description: Try three short lessons on original Noun portraits, companion states, and Bot Money art notes. The local quiz records your first answer to each question, explains the answer, and exports a learning card when you finish.
audience: Sketchbook keepers, gardeners, learners, and anyone building a gentle practice

companionBehavior.idle: Visual direction: A single seed mark rests below the Noun on a garden-like baseline.
companionBehavior.working: Visual direction: A leaf appears in one of seven surrounding slots when you manually record a visit.
companionBehavior.needsYou: Visual direction: An unfilled leaf outline offers an optional return; no warning or broken-streak mark appears.
companionBehavior.complete: Visual direction: Seven leaf slots form a wreath around the unchanged portrait for a finished practice card.

firstBuild: Three multiple-choice lessons, first-answer scoring, explanations, and a text learning card.
expansion: More small lessons, workshop packs, practice cards, and optional schedules for returning.
artifact: A text learning card with your first-answer score, correct answers, and all three explanations.
exampleTask: Learn what a Noun seed, a working-state signal, and an art denomination actually establish.
steps: Choose an answer to each question
futureConnection: Optional saved progress or reminders could be added after the user chooses them. This demo has no account, activity tracking, or scheduled reminders.

name: Beacon
description: Create a welcome card for a gathering using an occasion, a host, and your own welcome line. The local tool divides fifteen, thirty, or sixty minutes into arrival, shared activity, and closing; it sends no invitations.
audience: Small studios, project leads, event teams, and shared workspaces

companionBehavior.idle: Visual direction: A hollow signal ring sits behind the unchanged Noun with the label Ready.
companionBehavior.working: Visual direction: A steady blue perimeter and the written status In progress show active work.
companionBehavior.needsYou: Visual direction: An amber chevron and explicit Needs you label point to the entered next action.
companionBehavior.complete: Visual direction: The signal ring closes into a green square seal labeled Complete.

firstBuild: Occasion, host, welcome text, duration selector, three-part agenda, and a downloadable text card.
expansion: Printable place cards, workshop tickets, gathering-specific companion themes, and a small shared display.
artifact: A text welcome card and agenda whose three parts add up to the selected duration.
exampleTask: Plan a thirty-minute gathering to fold Nouns temples with friends.
futureConnection: An invitation or calendar connector could be added with explicit permission later. The demo does not invite guests, reserve spaces, or monitor attendance.

name: Harbor
tagline: A place to set your thoughts down.
description: Write an intention, a reflection, or both, then add a feeling and optional dedication. The local tool arranges your words into a text keepsake card; it generates no interpretation, advice, or prayer text.
audience: Gift givers, personal writers, and people making shrine or altar keepsakes

companionBehavior.idle: Visual direction: Two still waterlines frame the unchanged Noun with generous open space.
companionBehavior.working: Visual direction: The waterlines separate gently as your words fill the reflection card.
companionBehavior.needsYou: Visual direction: A small open envelope invites you to review the dedication before saving.
companionBehavior.complete: Visual direction: The waterlines meet a quiet horizon and a folded-card mark appears.

firstBuild: Feeling selector, intention and reflection fields, optional dedication, validation, and text-card export.
expansion: Matching shrine and altar editions, anniversary cards, shared family rituals, and gift-set packaging.
artifact: A text reflection card containing the words you entered, ready to adapt for a sanctuary keepsake.
exampleTask: Write a dedication for a friend beginning a new chapter.
futureConnection: A future explicit handoff could transfer the approved words into the sanctuary designer. The concept does not provide spiritual authority, send messages, or infer personal beliefs.

name: Relay
tagline: Pass the work with its context.
description: Assign three steps toward a shared goal, each with an owner and a definition of done. The local tool checks that the handoff is complete and exports a brief; it does not contact people or start agents.
audience: Collaborating makers, small teams, and people coordinating specialist bots

companionBehavior.idle: Visual direction: Two unconnected nodes flank the original Noun, leaving the route open.
companionBehavior.working: Visual direction: Three context tiles line up between the portrait and a labeled destination role.
companionBehavior.needsYou: Visual direction: The final connection remains visibly open while the handoff awaits your review.
companionBehavior.complete: Visual direction: A closed route and Saved packet label appear after export; no Sent claim is shown.

firstBuild: Shared goal and three task/owner/done groups, required-field validation, and text-brief export.
expansion: Team-specific handoff templates, versioned briefs, and a visible chain of accepted work.
artifact: A text handoff brief with three owners, acceptance criteria, and a clear prepared-locally status.
exampleTask: Prepare a handoff from a Nouns note designer to a print QA specialist.
steps: Give each step an owner and outcome
futureConnection: Actual dispatch would require an available agent or messaging connector and explicit authorization. The local demo prepares the packet without sending it.

name: Treasury
tagline: Make a token of the work.
description: Prepare a dedication and reverse message for a collectible Nouns Bot Money note. The local demo exports a text brief and links to the separate note studio, where original Nouns art and fictional denominations become printable keepsakes.
audience: Nouns collectors, bot builders, creative teams, and paper-money enthusiasts

companionBehavior.idle: Visual direction: An empty banknote frame rests behind the unchanged original Noun.
companionBehavior.working: Visual direction: Denomination, dedication, and edition fields settle into the surrounding note layout as you edit.
companionBehavior.needsYou: Visual direction: A proof-check marker highlights the final wording and trim before you export.
companionBehavior.complete: Visual direction: A collectible-art seal and edition serial complete the note; no wallet or payment state appears.

firstBuild: Fictional denomination, occasion, dedication, and reverse-message controls; a text brief; and a link to the note studio.
expansion: Companion-specific note families, task memento books, matching art stamps, and physical collector gift sets.
artifact: A Nouns Bot Money dedication brief; the separate studio provides the printable note and edition record.
exampleTask: Make a Bot Money note celebrating the first completed Noun companion prototype.
steps: Save the brief and open the note studio
futureConnection: A future edition registry could track print releases and provenance. These art notes do not create currency, credit, token ownership, redemption rights, or an automatic wallet connection.
